discovery: Discovery of magnetic skyrmions and their emergent electromagnetism in chiral magnets

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science, Japan

motivation: Pfleiderer and co-workers discovered, by neutron scattering in MnSi (2009), a lattice of magnetic skyrmions: topologically protected whirls of spin stabilized by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Tokura and co-workers then imaged individual skyrmions and skyrmion crystals in real space by Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (2010), found them at room temperature and in multiferroic insulators, and showed that they can be driven by electric currents a million times weaker than those needed for conventional domain walls. Together these discoveries established a new form of topological matter in solids. Through the Berry phase, skyrmions produce emergent magnetic and electric fields, which appear as the topological Hall effect and as skyrmion motion. The concept has spread to many materials, techniques and dimensions, opening the field of topological magnetism and pointing to low-power spintronic memory and logic.
